properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 16 at 6:00AM EDT by NWS Jackson KY
properties.description:
Plenty of sunshine and a dome of heat will sent temperatures into
the low to mid 90s for most of the area today and Thursday. When
combined with higher than normal humidities this results in heat
indices from 95 to 100 degrees for much of eastern Kentucky both
afternoons. There is only scant chances for showers or storms to
provide limited and localized relief through Thursday.

Try to limit time outdoors today during the afternoon, when heat
illness is most likely to occur. If going outdoors, drink plenty
of fluids and take breaks out of the sun.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued September 15 at 5:02PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...The Imperial County APCD has issued an air quality alert
due to increased fine particle pollution from wildfire smoke.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...Smoke from a fire in Mexico is moving towards western
Imperial County.. Levels of particle pollution can vary by time and
location depending on fire activity and local weather conditions.

* WHEN...tonight September 15 2026.

* IMPACTS...Particles in wildfire smoke can get deep into the lungs
and cause serious health problems such as heart attacks, strokes,
asthma attacks, and difficulty breathing. Everyone can be affected,
but people with lung or heart disease, older adults, people who are
pregnant, children, and those who spend a lot of time outdoors are
at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, if you smell or see smoke:

* Remain indoors with windows and doors closed
* Avoid intense outdoor physical activity
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* If you must be outdoors, keep the time brief and wear a well-
fitting N-95 mask
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: Lower Matanuska Valley; Hatcher Pass; Southern Susitna Valley; Central Susitna Valley
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 15 at 3:20PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
ESFAFC

Locations:

* Willow and Talkeetna
* Rivers, creeks, and streams with headwaters along the western
Talkeetna Mountains

Timing:

* Now through Wednesday (tomorrow) afternoon. Heaviest rainfall
expected from now through about midnight tonight.

Rainfall:

* The heaviest rain is ongoing. However, an estimated 1.5 to 2 inches
of rain have fallen along the Alaska Range and Talkeetna Mountains
so far today, with about 0.5 to 1 inches in Susitna Valley.
* Additional rainfall amounts of about 0.5 to 1.5 inches are forecast
from now through tomorrow afternoon.
* These rainfall totals likely won't be high enough for widespread
flooding, but smaller tributaries draining the Talkeetnas including
Willow Creek and the Little Susitna may reach bankfull.

Hydrologic Concerns:

* Many lower locations along rivers such as gravel bars and other
spots popular for camping and recreating may become inundated with
water with rivers reaching bankfull conditions.

* Heavy rain may result in localized ponding in low-lying areas and
locations with poor drainage.

Next Steps:

* Residents along area streams as well as river users and recreators
should anticipate higher than normal water levels and are advised
to monitor weather and river forecasts.

* Send weather or flooding reports to inws.ncep.noaa.gov/report/ or
by calling 1-907-266-5127.

* Reports on river conditions may be sent to the river forecast
center by calling 1-907-266-5160.
